title: Knowledge check: Applications of R in Different Industries

questions.prompt: For “Applications of R in Different Industries”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Applications of R in Different Industries is one step in Introduction to R; start with base R and short expressions. Separate displayed output from values returned by expressions. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Applications of R in Different Industries” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “Business Analytics and Finance” as part of lesson 3. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Applications of R in Different Industries” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Begin with console work; then move the same tested expressions into a saved script. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
